name: Aura Monitor — Designing for a 2.1-Inch Circle
context: A client engagement at Zemingo for Clearblue. Aura is a connected fertility monitor with a small round display, and the work was to decide what that display shows. Unlike the other confidential client work in this portfolio, Clearblue is named openly in the delivered case study, so the agent may name it.
role: Project lead, art direction, 3D model and viewer
summary: Three directions for the display of a connected fertility monitor, judged on the object rather than on a board. A flat frame cannot tell you how a screen reads inside a bezel, under glass, in a hand, at the one moment a test stick slides in. So the device was modelled in 3D and wrapped in an interactive viewer that loads any of the three directions onto it, turns it, zooms it and runs the test — which let nine screens be reviewed as a product before the product existed.
challenge: Nine screens in Figma can tell you whether they are tidy. They cannot tell you how each one reads inside the bezel, next to the others, in the order a user meets them. The brief for the model was therefore narrow and worth stating: not a manufacturing file, just believable enough that a reviewer stops looking at artwork and starts looking at a product.

evidence.label: Case study, as delivered
evidence.notes: The written case study: why the device was modelled, how the model was built, what the viewer made checkable, and the three directions side by side. The embedded recording was lifted out to /media so the page is not a megabyte of base64.

evidence.label: Interactive viewer
evidence.notes: The viewer itself, running: turn and zoom the device, switch between the three directions, start a test. Three analytics installers were removed before publication — two script tags and an inline loader — and the font stylesheet was repointed at Google Fonts, which is also what makes the page work standalone.

presentation.short_pitch: Three display directions for a connected fertility monitor, judged on a 3D model of the device instead of on a board.
presentation.long_pitch: Clearblue's Aura is a connected fertility monitor with a 2.1-inch round display. Boaz led the work at Zemingo on what that display shows: three directions, nine screens. Rather than review them as flat frames, the device was modelled in Blender and wrapped in an interactive viewer that loads any direction onto it — turn it, zoom it, slide the test stick in. That let the team check the things a frame hides: whether the circle holds, whether each background works, whether the moment reads, and whether it still feels related to the app.
suggested_followups: Want to open the viewer and turn the device, or read how the model was built?
I can also compare the three directions — App Based, Human Centered and Data Based.
